relevant_findings.topic: Rust is the PRIMARY repaint driver for exterior metal
relevant_findings.summary: Unlike wood/masonry RP where chalking and peeling are the primary drivers, metal RP is overwhelmingly driven by corrosion. Rust grade assessment (flash, moderate pitting, heavy scale) determines the entire prep scope. Rust assessment is the single most important RP-specific addition over NC.
relevant_findings.implication: Condition assessment module is MANDATORY first module. Rust grade directly drives prep task activation (SP2 vs SP3 vs needle gun), rust converter usage, and primer scope (spot vs full).

relevant_findings.topic: Three rust grades drive prep intensity
relevant_findings.summary: Flash rust (surface oxidation, orange discoloration, no pitting) requires SP2 hand tool cleaning. Moderate rust (visible pitting, scale beginning) requires SP3 power tool cleaning. Heavy rust/scale (deep pitting, thick scale deposits) requires needle gun or power scraper for mechanical removal. Structural rust (section loss, perforation) is a HARD STOP.
relevant_findings.implication: Rust grade maps to substrate states: SS_EXT_FLASH_RUST → SP2, SS_EXT_MODERATE_RUST → SP3, SS_EXT_HEAVY_RUST → needle gun + SP3. Structural rust is not a valid input state — it is a gate condition.

relevant_findings.topic: Multiple metal substrate types require different primer chemistry — same as NC
relevant_findings.summary: Carbon steel and wrought iron use DTM acrylic/alkyd primers. Galvanized steel requires etch primer (DTM alkyd is BLOCKED — saponification). Aluminum requires aluminum-compatible DTM or etch primer. Factory-finished non-ferrous uses bonding primer. These chemistry rules carry over from NC unchanged.
relevant_findings.implication: Substrate type dimension retained from NC. Primer routing logic identical. Compatibility rules COMPAT-METL-001 through COMPAT-METL-009 all carry over.

relevant_findings.topic: Rust converter is a RP-specific complementary treatment
relevant_findings.summary: Rust converter (phosphoric/tannic acid) converts unstable iron oxide to stable iron phosphate/tannate. Applied AFTER mechanical prep (SP2/SP3) to residual rust that cannot be fully removed. Not a replacement for mechanical prep. Single application with 24 hr cure before priming. Best for intricate profiles where power tool access is impossible (scrollwork, balusters). Shorter coating life (1-3 yr) vs full mechanical removal.
relevant_findings.implication: Rust converter task is RP-specific addition. It was already in NC spec as an option but becomes far more common in RP context. 24 hr cure requires separate mobilization or scheduling gap.

relevant_findings.topic: Sound existing paint on metal simplifies prep dramatically
relevant_findings.summary: When existing coating is sound (good adhesion, no rust, no peeling), RP metal requires only degloss scuff + spot prime exposed areas + 2 finish coats. This is the lightest RP scenario. DTM acrylic finish is self-priming on sound existing paint — spot prime only bare areas.
relevant_findings.implication: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT_METAL state results in minimal prep overhead. No full primer coat needed. Spot prime only. This is the maintenance repaint scenario — should be fastest variant.

relevant_findings.topic: QT range for metal RP is QT2-QT4
relevant_findings.summary: QT2 is appropriate for utility metal items (downspouts, HVAC line covers, vent covers) where economy prep is acceptable. QT3 is standard for most residential metal (railings, gutters). QT4 for decorative ironwork. QT5 excluded for RP — premium restoration-quality work on existing metal (zinc-rich primer, DFT verification, near-white blast) is impractical over existing coatings and should be quoted as NC strip-to-bare instead.
relevant_findings.implication: QT range QT2-QT4 differs from NC (QT3-QT5). QT2 added for utility items, QT5 removed because zinc-rich primer and near-white blast are incompatible with RP over existing coatings.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheens for metal RP are satin and semi-gloss
relevant_findings.summary: Gloss is excluded for RP. Gloss sheen requires substrate perfection not achievable over existing paint — brush marks, prep textures, and feathered edges are magnified at gloss level. Satin and semi-gloss provide adequate water shedding and UV protection for metal while hiding substrate imperfections.
relevant_findings.implication: Sheen dimension restricted to satin and semi-gloss. Follows garage door RP pattern (gloss excluded for same reason).

relevant_findings.summary: Brush is primary for metal RP because most metal RP involves many small discrete items requiring detail work. Spray is appropriate for long gutter runs and production work. spray_backbrush (NC method for ornamental profiles) is less common in RP because ornamental ironwork RP is typically brush-only due to existing coating inconsistencies. Roll is PROHIBITED on metal (same as NC).
relevant_findings.implication: Application methods: brush and spray. spray_backbrush dropped from RP — ornamental detail work on existing coatings is better served by brush-only to control film build on inconsistent substrates.

relevant_findings.topic: Many small items, mixed UOM — same 4 paintable items as NC
relevant_findings.summary: Metal RP involves the same physical items as NC: gutters (LF), downspouts (LF), railings (LF), ornamental iron (EA), misc discrete items (EA). The 4 paintable items from NC carry over unchanged. RP adds condition assessment per item but the counting/measurement model is identical.
relevant_findings.implication: Reuse all 4 ITM_ items from NC: ITM_METAL_RAILING, ITM_METAL_GUTTER, ITM_METAL_ORNAMENTAL, ITM_METAL_MISC. Same PS keys and IN inputs for quantities.

relevant_findings.topic: Environmental modifiers excluded for RP estimation
relevant_findings.summary: Wind, sun exposure, and surface temperature are scheduling constraints, not estimatable modifiers. Per PaintFactor OS RC-003, environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time and excluded from estimation. NC spec included them as informational — RP spec should exclude them entirely to match the RP pattern established by garage door RP and trim RP.
relevant_findings.implication: FAC_EXT_WIND, FAC_EXT_SUN_EXPOSURE, and FAC_EXT_SURFACE_TEMP are NOT included in RP spec. Only FAC_MTRP_PROFILE_COMPLEXITY, FAC_EXT_ACCESS, FAC_MTRP_QT, and FAC_MTRP_CONDITION are estimation modifiers.

relevant_findings.topic: RRP (lead paint) is very rare for metal items
relevant_findings.summary: Metal surfaces were rarely painted with lead-based paint by themselves. Lead paint on metal is uncommon but not impossible — pre-1978 decorative ironwork and railings may have lead paint. RRP gate should be present but is a low-probability trigger. When triggered, scope escalates to RRP-certified contractor.
relevant_findings.implication: Include pre_1978 flag and RRP gate check in assessment module, but do not model full RRP containment in this spec. If lead detected, escalate to RRP scope (separate spec/pricing).

relevant_findings.topic: Condition modifier drives RP prep cost variance
relevant_findings.summary: Condition (rust grade / coating failure extent) is the primary RP cost driver beyond profile complexity. Sound paint = 1.0x baseline. Flash rust = 1.25x (SP2 hand tool). Moderate rust = 1.60x (SP3 power tool). Heavy rust/scale = 2.25x (needle gun + SP3). Failing paint = 1.50x (strip + SP3). These modifiers apply to prep tasks only — coating tasks are uniform after prep normalizes the substrate.
relevant_findings.implication: FAC_MTRP_CONDITION modifier with 5 values. Applied to prep tasks only. Stacking pool: PREP_ONLY (condition + access). Coating pool: QT + access + profile complexity.

relevant_findings.topic: Substrate states for metal RP — 5 input states
relevant_findings.summary: RP metal has 5 valid input substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT_METAL (intact coating, good adhesion), SS_EXT_FLASH_RUST (surface oxidation, no pitting), SS_EXT_MODERATE_RUST (visible pitting, scale), SS_EXT_HEAVY_RUST (deep pitting, thick scale — not structural), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT_METAL (peeling, flaking, blistering). Structural rust is a HARD STOP, not a valid input state.
relevant_findings.implication: 5 substrate states drive 5 prep paths. Each state maps to specific prep task activation, primer scope, and condition modifier value.

relevant_findings.summary: Based on NC spec (37 tasks) adjusted for RP: add condition assessment module (+4 tasks for rust grading, adhesion test, coating ID, lead gate), add needle gun task (+1), add power wash task (+1), remove zinc-rich primer (-1, QT5 only), remove epoxy primer (-1, QT5/specialty), simplify environmental tasks (-3). Net: ~35-38 tasks.
relevant_findings.implication: Within the projected 30-40 task range from the brief.
sources: RP pattern analysis from garage door and trim RP specs

configuration_dimensions_proposed.notes: QT2 for utility items (downspouts, vent covers). QT3 standard residential. QT4 decorative ironwork. QT5 excluded — premium restoration requires NC strip-to-bare approach.
Retained from NC unchanged. Drives primer chemistry selection. Per-item capture for mixed-substrate projects.

Brush primary for detail work. Spray for production gutter runs. spray_backbrush dropped for RP. Roll PROHIBITED.
Gloss excluded for RP — substrate imperfections visible at gloss level.

material_systems_proposed.notes: Standard DTM for ferrous metal RP. Spot or full depending on condition.
Alkyd DTM for pitted ferrous. BLOCKED on galvanized/aluminum.
Etch primer for bare non-ferrous. Retained from NC.
Bonding primer for factory-finished/sound existing non-ferrous.
Universal DTM acrylic finish. 2 coats. Self-priming on sound existing paint.
Rust converter treatment. RP-specific. Applied after mechanical prep to residual rust.

research_corrections.original_claim: spray_backbrush should be retained from NC for ornamental profiles
research_corrections.corrected_to: spray_backbrush is impractical for RP ornamental work — existing coating thickness variations and condition inconsistencies make spray deposit control unreliable. Brush-only provides better film control on inconsistent RP substrates. Spray retained for production runs (gutters, straight railings).

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions should be estimation modifiers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable — unpredictable at bid time. Excluded from spec per PaintFactor OS RC-003.
